newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Auditor-general reports bad S.Africa govt controls.
newsitem.headline: Auditor-general reports bad S.Africa govt controls.

text.p: South African Auditor-General Henri Kluever warned parliament on Wednesday that inadequate management controls continued to allow for inefficient and uneconomical use of government resources.
In a report on eight specialist "performance audits" in the second half of last year, he said there was evidence of inconsistent planning, budget and procurement controls.

"These deficiencies and shortcomings impact negatively on value for money received by the taxpayer and the rendering of services, which would be of concern to taxpayers and their representatives in parliament," he said.
Kluever said his audit showed the 1990 survey of household expenditure, still the basis of the consumer price index, focused only on urban homes and excluded 51.3 percent of the population.
His report was based on in-depth studies of the efficiency, economy and effectiveness of six government departments.

Failings uncovered ranged from the inaccurate and incomplete Air Force management of aircraft components and spare parts worth over six billion rand to evidence that up to 63 percent of suburban passengers do not pay their way.
- The Department of Environment Affairs approved an anchovy catch last year of 200,000 tonnes, which was four times the maximum recommended by the Sea Fisheries Research Institute.
- Air Force stock worth 820 million rand in one store showed no movement in three years and elsewhere a two million rand consignment was paid for but never received.
- Central Statistical Service figures took up to five years to publish.
- The Meat Board paid 1.5 million rand for a red-meat promotion during a shortage and could not use the material.
Kluever's report listed corrective mechanisms promised in response to his findings but noted that in several departments, there was no evidence of improvement after previous audits.
